title: Burst credit scheduler, billing granularity, and owner-level slot limits
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Customers using Dedicated pools need predictable throughput guarantees but also occasional headroom for traffic spikes. Current temporary boost logic hands out fixed-duration capacity slices that are coarse-grained for billing (minute-level) and tracked at the pool level. That causes two problems: (1) per-customer short spikes cause whole-pool billing jumps and unclear invoice items, and (2) no owner-level soft limits exist to prevent a noisy workload from consuming remaining burst credits and degrading other tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a burst credit scheduler that allocates credits at owner (customer) granularity and supports fractional-second accounting for billing reconciliation
Expose an owner-level 'burst slot' limit that defaults to 25% of pool burst capacity and is configurable via console/API
Invoice line-items show per-owner temporary boost usage with timestamps (second-resolution) and human-readable reason tags
Autoscaler and admission path enforce preemption policy: canevict zero-cost queued requests from burst-only slots when capacity contention occurs
End-to-end latency regression < 5% on 99th percentile for steady-state traffic in bench runs with burst enabled
proposed_solution: We will implement a burst credit scheduler that tracks 'credits' per owner with a sliding window decay and a centralized allocator that issues short-lived burst leases (default 10s) charged in sub-minute billing units. The scheduler will: 1) maintain owner balances in Redis with TTL-based decay, 2) grant burst leases when pool has free burst capacity and owner balance > 0 or owner has 'auto-topup' enabled, and 3) decrement balances in micro-units to allow fine-grained billing reconciliation. To reduce blast radius from noisy tenants we will introduce an owner-level slot cap enforced by admission logic in the serving runtime; when an owner exceeds slots, requests are queued to dedicated reserved capacity or deprioritized. Billing pipeline will be extended to aggregate per-owner second-resolution events into invoice-friendly lines and to annotate Console usage UI with burst reasons and lease IDs.
api_changes: GET /v1/dedicated/pools/:pool_id/owners/:owner_id/burst-balance - read-only balance and recent lease history
Console: new UI panel 'Burst usage by owner' showing active leases, historical spikes, and invoice preview
telemetry: metric: burst.leases.granted (tags: pool_id, owner_id, lease_id, reason)
trace: lease-grant path with latency and decision reason
log: billing-event (lease_id, owner_id, seconds_charged, cost_estimate) exported to billing-events topic
